evals.prompt: Generate pytest unit tests for the parse_front_matter function in evals/files/validate_front_matter.py. Focus on the return values for valid files, files with no front matter, and files with malformed YAML.
evals.expected_output: A pytest file using parametrize with pytest.param(id=...), tmp_path fixture, AAA structure, and at least one assertion per test.
expectations: The generated test file contains at least one use of @pytest.mark.parametrize
Each parametrize call uses pytest.param with an id= keyword argument (e.g., id='valid-yaml' or id="valid-yaml")
At least one test function name follows the pattern test_<unit>_<scenario>_<expected_outcome> (contains at least three underscore-separated segments starting with test_)
The tests use tmp_path or a pytest fixture for creating temporary input files rather than hardcoded file paths
Every test function body contains at least one assert statement
The test file imports pytest at the top level

evals.prompt: Write pytest tests for the async function fetch_with_retry in evals/files/async_client.py. The function retries on HTTP 429 and 503 up to max_retries times with exponential backoff. Cover the success case, retry-then-succeed, max retries exceeded, and non-retryable status codes.
evals.expected_output: A pytest file using @pytest.mark.asyncio, spec'd mock objects, and pytest.raises for the error paths.
expectations: The generated test file contains at least one function decorated with @pytest.mark.asyncio
Mock objects for the HTTP client or session use spec= or autospec=True (grep for spec= or autospec=)
The test file covers at least three of these four scenarios: success on first attempt, success after retry, max retries exceeded raising an exception, non-retryable status code raising immediately
The test for max-retries-exceeded asserts that an exception is raised (uses pytest.raises)
The test file contains at least one use of @pytest.mark.asyncio decorator (not just an import — the decorator must appear in the test code)

evals.prompt: Run the unit tests in the tests/unit/ directory. Show me which tests pass and which fail, and give me a brief summary of the overall result.
evals.expected_output: Execution of pytest on tests/unit/ with a pass/fail count summary.
expectations: The transcript shows a Bash tool call that invokes pytest (e.g., pytest tests/unit or uv run pytest tests/unit)
The response includes a summary of how many tests passed and how many failed (contains digits followed by passed or failed)
The response does not generate new test code — it executes the existing suite

evals.prompt: Review the test quality of the existing tests in evals/files/weak_tests.py and provide specific, actionable feedback. Identify at least three concrete issues and suggest how to fix each one.
evals.expected_output: A review identifying at least 3 specific quality issues with test function names cited and concrete fixes provided.
expectations: The review identifies at least three distinct quality issues (numbered or bulleted list with at least 3 items)
The review mentions at least one issue related to assertion quality (e.g., assert True, asserting only that no exception is raised, or missing assertions)
The review mentions at least one issue related to parametrize or test duplication (similar tests that could be combined)
Each identified issue includes a concrete suggestion for how to fix it (not just add more tests)
The review references specific test function names (e.g., test_multiply or test_add_positive_again)

evals.prompt: Generate pytest tests for the validate_email function in evals/files/validators.py. This is a validation function — make sure to cover valid inputs, invalid inputs, boundary conditions, and None/empty inputs.
evals.expected_output: A pytest file using parametrize with pytest.param(id=...), covering None, empty string, valid, invalid, and boundary email inputs.
expectations: The generated test file uses @pytest.mark.parametrize with at least 3 parameter sets
The test file includes a test case for None input (the word None appears as a parameter value or in a pytest.param call)
The test file includes a test case for empty string input ('' or "" appears as a parameter value)
Every parametrize entry either uses pytest.param with id= OR the parametrize ids= argument is used to provide human-readable names
The test file contains at least one assert statement that checks a return value against True or False (not just assert result is not None)
